artist.name: Susan Czermak
artist.tagline: Watercolours of light, place and remembered moments
artist.subtitle: Painted from landscapes encountered across Australia, Europe and beyond
artist.bio: Susan Czermak is a watercolourist with a style that is colourful and bold. Her love of environments and their hues can be seen in her mood-filled paintings that capture everyday moments of interest. A lover of travelling, Susan has lived in Scotland, New Zealand, England, USA, France and Australia. A realist painter inspired by the impressionists, her artworks capture her observations from around the globe. With a focus on land and streetscapes and interest in exploring light and shade, her paintings reflect on places and moments of delight.
artist.bioExtended: Susan has lived in Scotland, New Zealand, England, the United States, France and Australia. She has worked as a computer programmer, farmer and teacher, and has been exploring watercolour for over twenty-five years. She lived for ten years in a village in south-west France and has held regular solo exhibitions since 2001, mainly in France. Her work is held in private collections across France, Italy, Germany, Holland, Belgium, Switzerland, the UK, USA, Canada, New Zealand and Australia. In 2022 she received the People's Choice Award at the Peninsula Studio Trail exhibition. Susan's studio is located in the Melbourne area of Victoria where she lives with her partner and two small dogs.
exhibitions: Peninsula Studio Trail Open Studios (annual participant)

artist.studioNote: Studio visits by arrangement during Peninsula Studio Trail open weekends and by appointment.

curatorialStatement: Susan paints places she has stood within — tidal flats, quiet farms, village streets and working landscapes — preserving less the exact detail than the light and feeling that remained.

artworks.title: Bridge at Nasbinals, Pilgrim Way to Compostela
artworks.story: The high Aubrac mountain plateau (SW France) is a stunning vast place full of historical remnants. Traces of buron summer huts, isolated farms, pilgrimage routes, waterways and lakes, tiny hamlets, churches, even an old pilgrim’s hospital. In the past the pilgrim route starting in Le Puy-en-Velay through Aubrac was the most important in France. In the clear skies of autumn the colour of the grassland can be vibrant. (Watercolor painted on handmade cotton paper from the Moulin de Larroque, SW France)
